necessaryCorrections.title: Scope registration commits stale ownership and state after reentry
necessaryCorrections.trigger: A normal DisplayObject subclass overrides protected assertUsable and reenters another Scope.use on the same node, or closes the original Scope during binding preflight.
necessaryCorrections.impact: Both Scopes can accept the same value; the outer call overwrites Engine/owner binding while both cleanup lists retain it. Closing during preflight still accepts the node into a closed and untracked Scope, leaking it past Engine shutdown.
necessaryCorrections.correction: Separate callback-capable preflight from a callback-free commit; revalidate Scope and Engine state, all Engine bindings, and root ownership immediately before committing. Guard same-value recursive registration and preserve the existing late-value and foreign-owner cleanup rules.
necessaryCorrections.basis: Explicit Scope owner uniqueness, cross-Engine binding, closing rejection and late-value cleanup contracts

necessaryCorrections.title: Mount commits into a disposed Stage after old-parent removal reentry
necessaryCorrections.trigger: A public container subclass calls Engine.dispose from its removeChild override while addChild reparents a live child to the Engine Stage.
necessaryCorrections.impact: The Stage finishes disposal before addChild commits, but addChild succeeds with one live child attached to the disposed Stage after the Engine closes.
necessaryCorrections.correction: Use internal non-virtual tree mutation operations after complete validation; keep user callbacks outside the atomic commit. If callbacks remain, revalidate terminal state, Engine state and both trees before mutation and prevent partial detach/binding on failure.
necessaryCorrections.basis: Explicit atomic mounting, no mounting while closing, and terminal-node contracts

necessaryCorrections.title: A still-open Scope leaks a new value rejected by its closing Engine
necessaryCorrections.trigger: During reverse Engine Scope shutdown, a newer Scope abort listener hands an already acquired unowned Releasable to an older Scope that has not entered closing yet.
necessaryCorrections.impact: Engine.assertOpen rejects before the value is registered or released; later Scope cleanup cannot find it.
necessaryCorrections.correction: Treat a Scope whose Engine is closing as closed for acceptance and retain safe late-value cleanup, or introduce a two-phase internal shutdown that closes every Scope to acceptance before callbacks run. Preserve old-value ordering and foreign owner/Engine protection.
necessaryCorrections.basis: Closing/late-value resource cleanup contract and reasonable expectation that Scope.use rejection during Engine shutdown still provides the same cleanup exit

necessaryCorrections.title: Failed cancellation registration leaves a live unreachable subscription
necessaryCorrections.trigger: An injected CancellationSignal.addEventListener throws after on inserts the subscription into its local Set.
necessaryCorrections.impact: on reports failure and returns no unsubscribe, but a subsequent event still invokes the handler.
necessaryCorrections.correction: Roll back local subscription state on any signal registration or post-registration check failure; attempt adapter rollback separately while preserving the primary error and any rollback error.
necessaryCorrections.basis: Independent unsubscribe semantics and reasonable failed-call atomicity for an injected cancellation port without a no-throw guarantee

necessaryCorrections.title: Listener removal failure skips child cleanup and the entire host shutdown
necessaryCorrections.trigger: A Stage subscription uses a CancellationSignal whose removeEventListener throws when Engine.dispose clears listeners.
necessaryCorrections.impact: Stage is marked terminal but its children remain live. Engine rejects with the raw error before host.stop, host.close or the close deadline runs; repeat disposal returns the same failed result and cannot resume cleanup.
necessaryCorrections.correction: Isolate each listener removal failure and continue remaining listener and child cleanup; collect diagnostics. Engine must aggregate Scope/Stage cleanup failures and still run host.stop and bounded host.close, rejecting with EgretError cause/cleanupErrors afterward. Keep successful host close as the only surface-release condition.
necessaryCorrections.basis: Explicit continue-cleanup-after-failure, bounded Engine shutdown, stable EgretError and safe-surface-return contracts

specCompliance.summary: The scoped names, package roles, pure-core type baseline, cancellation ordering, whole-dispatch event snapshots and success-only surface release are present. Reentry breaks ownership atomicity and terminal-state rejection; closing acceptance and cleanup failures have resource cleanup gaps.

strengths: Three real package responsibilities with contracts/runtime/engine dependency direction and no third-party runtime dependency
Unique close Promise cached before lifecycle callbacks and headless host ownership kept distinct
Whole-dispatch candidate snapshots, once removal before invocation and finally restoration
Behavior tests import the built public package and use independent literal expected traces
codeQuality.summary: Callback-capable operations separate validation from commit without revalidation, and a listener-cleanup exception can bypass the remaining Stage and host teardown. Required failures are demonstrated through normal public interfaces.
